rows: A fixed amount you must pay before the insurer pays any admissible claim. In indemnity plans, it is a threshold.
The insurer starts paying only after deductible is crossed.
A percentage of the admissible claim that you must bear. It does not reduce the sum insured, but reduces what insurer pays for that claim.
You share the bill in a fixed ratio, such as 0% or 20%.

A period after policy start during which certain claims are not payable. Standard policies generally have a 30-day initial waiting period and pre-existing-disease waiting periods are commonly capped at 36 months in newer IRDA-regulated.
